overview: The committee discussed boundary adjustments for the Boston Avenue and Tufts Institutional zoning districts, focusing on narrowing the project scope to the Hillside neighborhood. They also reviewed 40R smart growth overlays as a potential mechanism to secure millions in state reimbursement for the city's new high school project.

items.title: Zoning Presentation: Boston Avenue and Tufts Campus
items.summary: Innes Land Strategies Group presented existing land use, zoning, and Tufts University ownership maps to establish a baseline for the spring 2026 rezoning phase.

items.title: Boston Avenue Corridor Boundary Discussion
items.summary: The committee debated narrowing the district boundaries to focus on the Hillside commercial area while removing the southern Ball Square section to avoid policy conflicts and redundant study efforts.

items.title: Tufts Institutional District and Dover Amendment
items.summary: Director Alicia Hunt explained how the Dover Amendment limits local control over institutional uses and argued that campus-specific zoning would prevent legal inefficiencies regarding building heights and setbacks.

items.title: 40R Smart Growth Overlay Districts
items.summary: The committee explored adopting 40R zoning overlays to incentivize affordable housing, which could qualify the city for an estimated 1.5% reimbursement increase on the high school construction project.

items.title: Committee Requests and Public Comment
items.summary: Approved requests for the Innes team to draft revised Boston Avenue boundaries and for the planning office to research 40R overlay applications in Medford Square and Mystic Avenue. Public comment addressed university intentions and the impact of campus development on residential adjacencies.
